fabric-api:
Fabric API

Essential hooks for modding with Fabric.

Fabric API is the library for essential hooks and interoperability mechanisms for Fabric mods. Examples include:

- Exposing functionality that is useful but difficult to access for many mods such as particles, biomes and dimensions
- Adding events, hooks and APIs to improve interoperability between mods.
- Essential features such as registry synchronization and adding information to crash reports.
- An advanced rendering API designed for compatibility with optimization mods and graphics overhaul mods.

Also check out Fabric Loader, the (mostly) version-independent mod loader that powers Fabric. Fabric API is a mod like any other Fabric mod which requires Fabric Loader to be installed.

For support and discussion for both developers and users, visit the Fabric Discord server.

No Chat Reports

 

This mod strips cryptographic signatures which are attached to every chat message sent from 1.19 and onwards. Removing them makes it impossible to track and associate your chat messages with your Minecraft client, and, by extension, Microsoft account.

 As of 1.19.1, it also disables Player Chat Reporting 

Please notice that, while I am aware of Guardian and certain other exploits that allow you to counteract reporting systems on the client against the will of the server, I am consciously choosing to not integrate them as part of this mod. No Chat Reports will only remain effective on the client side if the server allows it to be. If you do not like servers that enforce chat signing and fully support chat reporting - I advise to simply not play on them.

healing-campfire:
Healing Campfire creates an area around the campfire where players and/or passive mobs receive the regeneration effect in a configurable radius. Modded passive entities will be healed as well as long as they are not classified as " EntityClassification.Monster ". When the entity has half of the remaining regeneration effect left and is near the campfire, the effect duration will refresh. Campfires added by other mods work as well. Mobs that are attacking a player won't be healed, and specific mobs can be excluded in the config. By default the campfire gives regeneration, but this can be changed to any other effect, or several at once. Soul campfires have their own radius, duration, level and effects, and can be set to heal hostile mobs instead. You may also be interested in No Hostiles Around Campfire .

ftb-quests-freeze-fix:
This is a simple fix mod for FTB Quests that caches the Quests menu on startup to prevent freezing in game. Tested in packs such as Prominence II RPG, where it prevents a 10 second lag spike when opening the quest book for the first time.

 How does this work?

FTB Quests needs to initialize Minecraft's Creative mode text search provider, which is not done by default in survival Minecraft since it's never used. This involves looping over every item in the game, fetching all of the tooltip contents, and processing them all. In large modpacks, with lots of items and quests, this scales up exponentially with more mods that add more text to items.

2032-world-height:
Increase the build limit to Y=2031 in all dimensions. 
 WARNING : Starting with Minecraft 1.21.2 removing the datapack/mod will corrupt your world! You can find a tutorial on how to remove it safely here.

 Does this support custom world generation mods/datapacks?
This datapack doesn't change world generation by itself, but custom world generation mods/datapacks may hardcode the world height. A notable example is Tectonic. The mod version of it is not supported, but if you're using the datapack version you go to /data/minecraft/dimension type/overworld.json inside the Tectonic datapack folder and change "logical height" and "height" to 2096.

 Does this work with existing worlds?
Officially no, but you can follow this tutorial to transfer existing chunks to a world made with this datapack.

custom-default-world-preset:
Custom Default World Preset
This simple fabric mod allows you to change the default world preset. 
This mod is intended for modpack developers who want a custom world without replacing the default and without making users change the setting.

To configure the default world preset you edit the default world preset.txt file in your config directory.
It should contain the id of the desired default preset. The minecraft: prefix may be omitted.
The configuration is read each time the key is used, so changes should show up be reopening the world creation screen.

This mod also changes the default on dedicated servers. You need to ensure that the preset is loaded in the initial datapacks for this to work.
Most global datapack mods should work for this.

Super Enchants

 Super Enchants allows you to combine enchantments to much higher levels than you're able to do normally in survival mode.

 How to Combine Enchantments

Throwing 2 enchanted books on top of an anvil will combine them. If they have the same enchantment at the same level, the new enchanted book they create will have that enchantment at the next level. And if you throw an enchantment book and an enchantable item on top of an anvil, that enchantment will be applied to the item, removing the need for experience levels.

 Extra Item Compatibility (MC 1.20.5 and Newer)

block-event-separator:
Block Event Separator allows you to see the inner workings of your piston contraptions by separating block events in real-time. While server-side behavior is perfectly preserved, on the client block events are separated by 1gt worth of time, allowing you to see the order in which pistons extend and/or retract within any tick. 

The mod can be activated in three modes using the /blockeventseparator mode command:

- depth : Block events are separated by depth (colloquially known as "microticks" or "BED"). Block events at the same depth start animating simultaneously.
- index : Block events are separated by index, based on the order in which they were executed. Each block event starts after the previous.
- block : Moving blocks are separated by index, based on the order in which they were created.

The pace at which the game steps through the block events can be changed using the /blockeven

Trajectorys

Trajectorys is a client-side Minecraft (Fabric) mod that predicts and visually displays the trajectory of projectiles such as bows, crossbows, and throwable items.
It allows you to confirm the impact point and trajectory before using an item, supporting precise shooting and throwing.

 Main Features

 1. Trajectory Rendering

When holding an item, the predicted parabolic path of the projectile is displayed as a line.

 It is calculated in real-time considering the viewing angle, charge time (e.g., bow draw), and player movement speed.

 Resistance in water is also included in the calculation.

 2. Hit Box Rendering

The impact point at the end of the predicted trajectory is highlighted with a box.

 Block Hit: Displays a box on the surface of the block.

 Entity Hit: Displays a box surrounding the entity if it is predicted to hit a mob or player.

 3. Show Flying Projectiles

pause-day-cycle:
Pause Day Cycle

 To enable AFK detection feature, Detect AFK Players must be installed. 

When nobody's on a Minecraft server, the in-game time still increases. This means you can't track the number of days played, and the local difficulty will also increase. That's not a concern for servers that have players online almost constantly, but for small/medium sized servers, this is a problem.

This is a very light-weight data pack to prevent game time from increasing when nobody's online or when every player online is tagged as afk , without pausing the server itself so that automatic farms can continue to run.

 
 See it in action 
 
 

Time pauses while player is AFK. Player sitting done with AFK Sit.

 

 Why another one of these?

invasive-optimizations:
Invasive Optimizations

 

Invasive optimizations for other mods, aiming to reduce server-side (tick) lag. 
The invasive nature of these changes makes them more likely to crash or otherwise break. 
Please report such issues to the issue tracker and I will try to respond to them in a timely manner. 
Each change can also be individually toggled through the config and should solve any issues temporarily while you wait for a fix.

Optimizations included in this mod fall under one of the following categories:
1. Patch has been sent but has not reviewed for a long time or expected to be useful in the time before the next release.
2. Patch denied due to reasons unrelated to quality.
3. Patch has no avenue of contribution (e.g. closed source mods)
4. Patch already applied but not available in released versions.

the-wizarding-world:
The Wizarding World
 
 

 

 Spell writing
 
 

Writing spells is no easy task. As a Pupil, 30 levels of experience (consumes 10) are needed in order to write a spell. A book and quill are required and a respective ingredient for each spell book.

 

As a Teacher, 15 levels are consumed in order to write a spell.

 

As a Master, 20 levels are consumed to write a spell.

 Wands

 

In order to cast any spells, you need a wand. There are three levels of wands. Pupil, Teacher, and Master. With each higher level wand, the previous level of spells will become stronger when casted and higher level spells will be available.

 Mana

Inertia! replaces the rigid, snapping camera of vanilla Minecraft with a silky-smooth, responsive system. It removes the harsh micro-stutters and "stair-stepping" of vanilla movement, replacing them with fluid transitions.

- Tired of micro-jitters from your mouse? Filter the noise. 
- Suffer from motion sickness? Stabilize your view.

The  Verdant Growth  is an unstoppable plant infection that spreads across the world, consuming forests and reshaping landscapes. It expands through two primary mechanisms: strangler vines entwine and overgrow trees, and underground roots transform even deepslate into lush greenery. This relentless overgrowth introduces new resources, challenges, and dangers; survival can be difficult, but the rewards are well worth it. Players may rarely find Imbued Heartwood , a key step in creating rapidly self-repairing equipment.

 Controls

autologinmod:
Languages

EN/English ZH-CN/简体中文

 Auto Login

A client-side Fabric mod that automatically logs you into authentication-based Minecraft servers (e.g. EasyAuth, AuthMe) using a locally encrypted password.

This mod runs entirely on the client and does not modify any server behavior.

 Features

- Automatically sends /login after joining a server
- Password is stored locally and encrypted (AES-GCM with random device key)
- No server-side plugin or mod required
- Client-only and suitable for multiplayer servers
- Manual command trigger for testing or fallback use

 Commands

 Set password (required once)

 text
/autologin set 
 

- Encrypts and saves the password locally
- Enables auto-login automatically

 Trigger auto-login immediately

 text
/autologin login
 

- Runs a login attempt immediately
- Useful for testing or manual retries

 Enable / disable

 text
/autologin on
/autologin off

armor-notifier:
The Mod

This mod's idea is simple: it will alert you whenever your armour is about to break. It works by checking every tick if the ratio between the current durability of your armour and the max durability of your armour is less than a user-defined percent value.

It also plays a fun little sound every time this alert is triggered.

You do not need any other mods to run this one, it is completely independent of any other libraries.

 How can I change the settings of the mod?

You can do this by typing /armornotifications in chat and hitting enter. This will bring you to the configuration screen, where you can change the settings you want and hit "done" when you're, well, done.

 Credits

A huge thanks goes out to Jan for helping me with the custom config screen, whose discord server can be found here. Also thanks to lwes (discord handle: lwes ) for helping me with the icon for the mod.

describes the chestplate slot of the inventory.

macos-chat-fixes:
macOS Chat Fixes

Fixes Minecraft's text fields (chat, sign editing, world names, search boxes, etc.) to behave like a native macOS text field: proper ⌘ and ⌥ arrow key navigation, word-aware selection, and macOS-style deletion instead of Windows/Linux key bindings pretending to be Mac shortcuts.

 The problem

Vanilla Minecraft only really understands one set of non-Mac text shortcuts: Ctrl+Arrow to jump by word, Ctrl+A/C/V/X for select/copy/paste/cut. On macOS, it maps ⌘ onto those same Ctrl-shaped shortcuts which gets arrow navigation wrong . On macOS:

- ⌘ + Left/Right should jump to the start/end of the line.
- ⌥ + Left/Right should jump by word, vanilla doesn't bind this at all on Mac.

This mod fixes all of that, without touching anything on Windows or Linux.

macOS聊天修复 修正了Minecraft的文本字段（聊天、符号编辑、世界名称、搜索框等），使其行为类似于原生macOS文本字段：正确的和箭头键导航、单词识别选择以及macOS风格的删除，而不是假装是Mac快捷键的Windows/Linux键绑定。 问题 Vanilla Minecraft只理解一组非Mac的文本快捷键：Ctrl + Arrow用于按词跳转，Ctrl + A/C/V/X用于选择/复制/粘贴/剪切。在macOS上，它会将映射到Ctrl形的快捷键上，这会导致箭头导航错误。 - + Left/Right应该跳转到行的开头/结尾。 - +左/右应该按单词跳转，vanilla在Mac上根本不绑定这个。 这个模组修复了所有这些，而不需要在Windows或Linux上碰任何东西。

cancelchat-fabric:
CancelChat

Prevent chat messages sent by players from appearing to other players.

 Players

This mod should not be installed on the client. Players do not need it.

 Standalone servers

This mod could technically be used to disable the chat on standalone Fabric servers — but messages will still be sent to the server console. This may be useful if a mod relies on chat input for data entry.

 Proxies (Bungeecord, Velocity, etc.)

This mod is intended to be installed on your backend Fabric servers. It prevents messages from being broadcast to other players, but still allows the message to be processed by the server.

It is intended for situations where a chat handling plugin (i.e. HuskChat) is used on your proxy, but you still need messages to be passed through to your backend server, e.g. for Discord Integration.

For Spigot servers, see this plugin).

This pack also includes useful quality-of-life mods like JourneyMap, Mouse Tweaks, Controlling, Full Brightness Toggle, NoFog, Mod Menu, and Zume. The goal is to keep the game close to vanilla while improving FPS, responsiveness, memory usage, visibility, controls, and general playability.

This modpack does not add new dimensions, mobs, weapons, or major gameplay content. It is mainly designed for players who want a cleaner, faster, and more convenient Minecraft experience. Performance results may vary depending on your hardware

Download the .zip file (do not unzip it).

Enable Better

VanitasPBR
 Full vanilla LabBPR textures for shaders

 Why was it made?

With plenty of help from the amazing people of the ShaderLabs Discord server(Especially Null (Author of Shrimple and Textureless) and JoaquiX (Author of AVPBR and https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/prime-resolution-x32)) and the ShaderLabs website, I began hand drawi

auralite-shaders:
🌌 AuraLite Shaders (Minecraft 1.16 – 26.3)

 ⭐ 65,000+ downloads across CurseForge & Modrinth — thank you!

 

 AuraLite is a modern, lightweight, and highly optimized shader pack built on top of the OpenGL 4.6 / GLSL 460 standard. It is specifically designed and tested for Minecraft 1.16 – 26.3 with Sodium + Iris (and compatible with OptiFine , Oculus ). Since v1.2.0 the cloud deck is a physically parameterised volumetric medium rather than a stack of painted layers, and every development instrument has been removed from the shipped code.

Paper plugin to prevent a villager monopoly by locking what a villager trades after its UI is opened.

WORKING: 1.21.x, 1.20.6 (Folia)
 
 (If you find out it works on another version shoot me a dm at Lupancham on discord with the version(s) and server software(s) : ) 

 Why do I need this?
 Thats a great question! Ask yourself, would it be best to limit a potential threat to a server economy? If yes, this plugin might be for you as this plugin allows you to stop villager re-rolling!

 How Does this Work?
 This works by checking if a villager has less than 1 xp, if so it will give tha villager 1 xp to lock its trades when a player opens its menu.
